subject: Chemistry
text: (a) Explain in three of four sentences how a soap is able to dissolve in water and the process of “cleaning” a greasy plate using this soap once it is dissolved. Diagrams may be used. [3 marks] (b) List three major differences between soaps and detergents. i. ii. iii. [3 marks]
html:
(a) Explain in three of four sentences how a soap is able to dissolve in water and

the process of “cleaning” a greasy plate using this soap once it is dissolved. Diagrams may be used.

[3 marks]

(b) List three major differences between soaps and detergents.

i.

ii.

iii.

[3 marks]
answerHtml:
(a) Soap anions have a polar ionic carboxylate head and a non-polar hydrocarbon tail. The head interacts with water by ion–dipole attractions while tails interact with grease by dispersion forces. Micelles disperse grease droplets with tails inward and heads toward water, allowing rinsing (3 marks).

(b) Three valid differences (3 marks): soaps are fatty-acid carboxylate salts; many detergents have sulfate/sulfonate heads. Soaps form insoluble scum with Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ in hard water; common synthetic detergents remain effective. Soap is protonated to a poorly soluble fatty acid in acidic water; many sulfonate detergents remain effective. Other scientifically valid comparisons may be accepted; avoid treating all detergents as identical.

subject: Chemistry
text: The cling plastics used in kitchens to wrap food were originally made from PVC (polyvinyl chloride – IUPAC name polycholorethene). However there were concerns about the possible toxicity and leaching of plasticisers added to the PVC to produce the thin flexible film. As a result, this material is now made predominantly from LDPE (low density polyethene), even though in this form it is less “clingy” than PVC. (a) What properties of LDPE make it suitable for use as a cling film? (b) Draw a partial structure for LDPE and PVC showing at least six carbons in the backbone. (c) Why would LDPE be less “clingy” than PVC? [5 marks]
html:
The cling plastics used in kitchens to wrap food were originally made from PVC (polyvinyl chloride – IUPAC name polycholorethene). However there were concerns about the possible toxicity and leaching of plasticisers added to the PVC to produce the thin flexible film. As a result, this material is now made predominantly from LDPE (low density polyethene), even though in this form it is less “clingy” than PVC.

(a) What properties of LDPE make it suitable for use as a cling film?

(b) Draw a partial structure for LDPE and PVC showing at least six carbons in the backbone.

(c) Why would LDPE be less “clingy” than PVC?

[5 marks]
answerHtml:
(a) LDPE is transparent, flexible, easily formed into thin film and suitable for wrapping food (any two relevant properties, 2 marks).

(b) LDPE backbone: …–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–… with representative short hydrocarbon branches. PVC backbone: …–CH₂–CHCl–CH₂–CHCl–CH₂–CHCl–… . Draw all bonds/atoms requested (2 marks).

(c) PVC has polar C–Cl bonds and stronger permanent dipole interactions; LDPE is essentially non-polar and relies on dispersion forces, so it is less clingy (1 mark).

subject: Chemistry
text: Consider the structure of Kevlar, nylon 6,6 and nylon 6,10: Kevlar Nylon 6,6 Nylon 6,10 a. What is common to each of these polymers? b. Which one of nylon 6,6 and nylon 6,10 would you expect to be more flexible? c. Which one of nylon 6,6 or nylon 6,10 would you expect to be stronger when used as a rope or fibre? d. Kevlar is used in bullet-proof vests, what about the structure of Kevlar makes it suitable for this use? [5 marks]
html:
Consider the structure of Kevlar, nylon 6,6 and nylon 6,10:

Kevlar

Nylon 6,6

Nylon 6,10

a. What is common to each of these polymers?

b. Which one of nylon 6,6 and nylon 6,10 would you expect to be more flexible?

c. Which one of nylon 6,6 or nylon 6,10 would you expect to be stronger when used as a rope or fibre?

d. Kevlar is used in bullet-proof vests, what about the structure of Kevlar makes it suitable for this use?

[5 marks]
answerHtml:
(a) All are polyamides / condensation polymers with amide links (1 mark).

(b) Nylon 6,10 is more flexible because its longer hydrocarbon sections can rotate more freely between amide links (1 mark).

(c) Nylon 6,6 has more amide links per unit chain length and stronger interchain hydrogen bonding per comparable length, giving greater fibre strength in this comparison (1 mark).

(d) Kevlar’s rigid aromatic rings and amide groups allow strong, aligned chains with extensive interchain hydrogen bonding, giving high tensile strength (2 marks).

subject: Chemistry
text: Valine, lysine and serine are three amino acids, which can combine to form proteins. (a) Draw the primary structure of a simple protein made from these amino acids (VAL-LYS-SER) (See data book for structures of amino acids). [2 marks] (b) Given the primary structure above, describe some of the interactions that would occur between chains of this protein in the tertiary structure. [3 marks]
html:
Valine, lysine and serine are three amino acids, which can combine to form proteins.

(a) Draw the primary structure of a simple protein made from these amino acids (VAL-LYS-SER) (See data book for structures of amino acids).

[2 marks]

(b) Given the primary structure above, describe some of the interactions that would occur between chains of this protein in the tertiary structure.

[3 marks]
answerHtml:
Teacher review required. The handwritten guide assigns an –OH group to lysine. The adapted answer uses the correct lysine amino side chain and serine hydroxyl side chain.

(a) H₂N–CH[CH(CH₃)₂]–C(=O)–NH–CH[(CH₂)₄NH₂]–C(=O)–NH–CH(CH₂OH)–COOH (2 marks for order VAL–LYS–SER and peptide links).

(b) Valine’s non-polar side chain can participate in hydrophobic/dispersion interactions. Lysine’s basic side chain can be protonated and form ionic attractions with negatively charged groups, and can hydrogen-bond. Serine’s –OH forms hydrogen bonds (one valid interaction per residue, 3 marks).

The scan describes lysine as having –OH; lysine has an amino group, whereas serine has –OH.
sourceReviewNotes: The handwritten guide assigns an –OH group to lysine. The adapted answer uses the correct lysine amino side chain and serine hydroxyl side chain.

subject: Chemistry
text: Ethanol is increasingly becoming a viable fuel alternative for a wide variety of applications. It has a number of production methods. a. Name the two types of chemical reaction through which ethanol is produced. i. ii. [2 marks] b. Write the oxidation and reduction half equations for the fermentation of glucose to water, ethanol and carbon dioxide. [2 marks] c. Write a general equation for the production of biodiesel using ethanol rather than the traditional methanol. [2 marks]
html:
Ethanol is increasingly becoming a viable fuel alternative for a wide variety of applications. It has a number of production methods.

a. Name the two types of chemical reaction through which ethanol is produced.

i.

ii.

[2 marks]

b. Write the oxidation and reduction half equations for the fermentation of glucose to water, ethanol and carbon dioxide.

[2 marks]

c. Write a general equation for the production of biodiesel using ethanol rather than the traditional methanol.

[2 marks]
answerHtml:
(a) Fermentation of glucose and hydration/addition of water to ethene (2 marks).

(b) One valid half-equation pair: oxidation C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6H₂O → 6CO₂ + 24H⁺ + 24e⁻; reduction C₆H₁₂O₆ + 12H⁺ + 12e⁻ → 3C₂H₅OH + 3H₂O (2 marks).

Combining one oxidation with two reductions and dividing by three gives C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂.

(c) Triglyceride + 3CH₃CH₂OH ⇌ glycerol + 3 fatty-acid ethyl esters (catalyst). General formula: C₃H₅[OC(=O)R]₃ + 3C₂H₅OH ⇌ C₃H₅(OH)₃ + 3RC(=O)OC₂H₅ (2 marks).
